title: Closed Mixed-Apparatus Compression of Schur Channels: Exact-Approximate Separation and Scheduled Delivery
description:
Preprint by Seth Douglas (seth.douglas@gmail.com). A finite closed mixed-apparatus construction approximates any Schur channel of Gram rank k in half-diamond distance using a physical apparatus of dimension of order epsilon^-2 (sqrt(k) + ln d), with a maximally mixed initializer of rank of order sqrt(k). A universal entropy converse 2Q - P >= S(J) and an exact extreme-channel cost P, Q >= log2 k give, for a known extreme rank-two ququart Schur channel, a matched leading-order exact-versus-vanishing-error separation: exact service needs P = Q = T, while error T^-4 admits Q = T/2 + O(log T) and P = O(log T). A separately scoped scheduled-delivery theorem compares sublogarithmic and superlogarithmic delay under mandatory arrivals, a common release schedule and observation-only stopping. Includes the complete manuscript, TeX source, reproducibility scripts and partial Lean coverage.

Lean coverage is partial: fourteen scoped dependency closures, not the headline analytic theorems. The construction is a probabilistic existence proof; no efficient compiler, arbitrary-channel upper bound, caller-paced delivery guarantee or sharp logarithmic-delay frontier is claimed. AI assistance is disclosed in the manuscript. This is a separate sequel to the closed repeated-use memory paper, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22779673.
